claims.claim: Right now, two things from the Sun's core are reaching the Earth. (Hook, A4: what a viewer who leaves at second two takes away.)
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'); https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.05379 (BX-P, full text)
claims.note: The two are the neutrinos and the fusion energy. MSFC: core reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'; neutrinos 'pass right through the overlying layers of the Sun and, with some effort, can be detected here on Earth'. BX-P: neutrinos 'travel almost undisturbed from the core of the Sun to the surface of the Earth'. A viewer who swipes at second two hears only that something from the core reaches the Earth right now, which is true for both, day and night ('the Earth', not 'you'). Nothing false is left behind; the photons themselves are not claimed to come from the core (the script later says 'the energy').

claims.claim: One left the core about eight minutes ago.
claims.note: Recomputed: radius 695,700 km / c = 2.32 s out of the Sun; mean distance 149.6e6 km minus radius / c = 497 s (8.28 min); 8.14-8.42 min from perihelion (147.1e6 km) to aphelion (152.1e6 km). Total about 8.3 min. Neutrinos move at c to better than 1e-8 (KATRIN m < 0.8 eV/c^2 at 90% CL; gamma > 1.25e4 even at 10 keV). 'About eight minutes' holds.

claims.claim: The other left it tens of thousands of years ago, maybe far more.
claims.source_checked: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin of Light'); https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1992ApJ...401..759M (Mitalas & Sills, ApJ 401, 759-760, both scan pages read; doi:10.1086/172103 metadata via api.crossref.org); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. Mitalas & Sills: 'diffusion time scale for the Sun of t_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr' (to the inner edge of the convection zone; abstract also calls 3e3-3e4 yr 'much too short'). MSFC: 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Lowest cited figure 4e4 yr, others 1.7e5 and ~1e6, so 'tens of thousands, maybe far more' is the narrowest reading all support (A3). What 'left' is the energy (MSFC 'This energy diffuses outward'). Stix 2003 not opened; nothing spoken depends on it.

claims.claim: Both start where hydrogen fuses into helium.
claims.note: MSFC: 'The Sun's core is the central region where nuclear reactions consume hydrogen to form helium.' BX-P eq. (1): '4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2 nu_e', the 'effective reaction' converting hydrogen into helium.

claims.claim: Every second, the Sun turns over four million tonnes of its mass into energy.
claims.note: NSSDC: 'Mass conversion rate (10^6 kg/s) 4260.' = 4.26 million tonnes/s. Cross-check: luminosity 382.8e24 W / c^2 = 4.259e9 kg/s. 'Four million' rounds down, so it does not overstate.

claims.claim: And every time four hydrogen nuclei become one helium nucleus, two neutrinos are made.
claims.note: BX-P eq. (1): '4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2 nu_e', 'with a net release of kinetic energy and emission of electron neutrinos'. p = hydrogen nucleus. MSFC first step: 'two protons collide to produce deuterium, a positron, and a neutrino'.

claims.claim: Neutrinos barely interact with anything.
claims.note: BX-P: 'they can only interact via the weak force. Thus, they travel almost undisturbed from the core of the Sun to the surface of the Earth'. MSFC: 'These elusive particles pass right through the overlying layers of the Sun'.

claims.claim: They fly straight out of the Sun in about two seconds.
claims.note: Recomputed: 695,700 km / 299,792,458 m/s = 2.32 s from the centre; from the core edge (MSFC: 175,000 km from centre) (695,700-175,000) km / c = 1.74 s. Speed = c to <1e-8 (KATRIN 'm_nu < 0.8 eV c^-2 at 90% CL'; BX-P pp endpoint 420 keV; at 10 keV gamma = 1.25e4, 1-v/c = 3e-9). 'Straight': MSFC 'pass right through', BX-P 'almost undisturbed'. 'About two seconds' holds for 1.7-2.3 s.

claims.claim: Eight minutes later, they reach the Earth, and pass through you.
claims.note: Surface to Earth 8.14-8.42 min, mean 8.28 min (recomputed from NSSDC distances and c). 'Pass through you': particles that 'pass right through the overlying layers of the Sun' (MSFC) and 'travel almost undisturbed' (BX-P) to a detector under the Gran Sasso pass through a body; implied by both, not stated in the words 'through you'.

claims.claim: Tens of billions of them cross every square centimetre of you, every second.
claims.note: BX-P: 'we can calculate the pp neutrino flux to be (6.6 +- 0.7) x 10^10 cm^-2 s^-1', and SSM pp flux 5.98-6.03 x 10^10 cm^-2 s^-1. pp alone is ~60-66 billion per cm^2 per second; 'tens of billions' is the narrower reading. Per cm^2 facing the Sun (standard flux convention).

claims.claim: In Italy, a detector called Borexino counted the ones from fusion's very first step.
claims.note: BX-P: 'Borexino is a liquid scintillator detector located at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso, in central Italy.' BX-N abstract: 'The primary reaction is thought to be the fusion of two protons with the emission of a low-energy neutrino ... Here we report spectral observations of pp neutrinos'. MSFC calls p+p the 'first step'. 'Counted': the result is a rate from a spectral fit, reported in counts per day ('c.p.d. per 100 t'), so 'counted' matches the paper's unit; no individual event is claimed identified.

claims.claim: In every hundred tonnes of its liquid, it caught about a hundred and forty a day.
claims.note: BX-P eq. (2): 'R_pp = 144 +- 13 (stat) +- 10 (syst) (d . 100 t)^-1'; Extended Data Fig. 8 'our reported value of 144 c.p.d. per 100 t'. Liquid: 'a liquid scintillator detector'. Rate is normalised to 100 t (fiducial mass was 75.5 t), which is what 'in every hundred tonnes' says. 'About 140' for 144.

claims.claim: The energy takes the slow road.
claims.source_checked: as claims 2, 3, 8 (SVS 11084, MSFC interior, Mitalas & Sills 1992, NSSDC, NIST)
claims.note: Comparative only: >= 4e4 yr against ~8 min. No new figure.

claims.claim: It is absorbed and given off again, over and over, then carried up by churning gas.
claims.note: SVS: 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. MSFC: energy moves 'by radiation ... through the radiative zone and by convective fluid flows (boiling motion) through the convection zone, the outermost 30%'; 'These convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'. Mitalas & Sills: 'In the solar convective zone, however, the energy transfer is by convection'. 'Churning gas' = MSFC's boiling fluid (surface density ~1/10,000 of air).

claims.claim: Tens of thousands of years later, maybe far more, it leaves the surface as sunlight.
claims.note: As claim 3 (4e4 / 1.7e5 / ~1e6 yr). MSFC: 'the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'.

claims.claim: Eight minutes after that, it lands on your skin.
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth 8.14-8.42 min, mean 8.28 min (recomputed).

claims.claim: So the sunlight shows what the core was doing when that energy set out.
claims.note: Follows from claims 3/15 and MSFC (core energy is what leaves as light). BX-P frames the same logic: agreement 'justifies the assumption made by the SSM that the photon and neutrino luminosities from the Sun can be correlated; i.e., that the Sun has been stable for the past 10^5 years', i.e. the photon luminosity reflects core output one transit time earlier.

claims.claim: The neutrinos show what it was doing eight minutes ago.
claims.note: 2.3 s + 8.3 min: neutrinos arriving now were made ~8.3 min ago; 'eight minutes ago' is the rounding.

claims.claim: In twenty fourteen, Borexino's count matched what the sunlight predicts, to within about ten percent.
claims.note: Date: BX-N published 27 Aug 2014. Prediction: BX-P 'expected rate of pp-induced electron recoils in Borexino to be 131 +- 2 (d.100 t)^-1 (assuming the high-metallicity SSM)'; measured 144 +- 13 +- 10. 144/131 = 1.099 (9.9% apart); combined error sqrt(13^2+10^2) = 16.4 (11%), so they agree within ~0.8 sigma; flux 6.6 vs 6.03 = 9.5% apart, +-0.7 = 10.6%. 'What the sunlight predicts' = the SSM expectation, which BX-P ties to the photon luminosity ('the assumption made by the SSM that the photon and neutrino luminosities from the Sun can be correlated'). 'Matched ... to within about ten percent' holds both as difference and as precision.

claims.claim: So the core is burning about as hard now as when today's sunlight set out.
claims.note: BX-P: 'the present measurement of the pp neutrino flux is consistent with expectation [which] justifies the assumption ... that the Sun has been stable for the past 10^5 years.' The script avoids BX-P's 10^5-yr figure and states the comparison relative to the sunlight's own departure time, which is the logic of BX-P's sentence whatever the transit time. 'About as hard' = within the ~10% precision (claim 19). 'Burning' = MSFC's own 'nuclear burning'.

claims.claim: The sunlight on your skin is old news. The neutrinos are fresh. And they agree.
claims.note: Restatement of claims 3/15 (>= tens of thousands of years), 9/18 (~8 min) and 19 (agreement within ~10%). No new figure.

claims.claim: 2 THINGS, 1 CORE
claims.note: Same content as claim 1.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES AGO / 8 MIN (neutrino lane clock); NEUTRINOS beside 8 MINUTES AGO
claims.note: ~8.3 min recomputed; '8' is the rounding.

claims.claim: 40,000+ YEARS AGO / 40,000+ YEARS (coral lane clock; running year counter climbing to 40,000+ YEARS and stopping); SUNLIGHT: THEN beside 40,000+ YEARS AGO
claims.where: on-screen: sunlight lane tags and year counter
claims.note: 40,000 = SVS, the lowest cited figure; '+' covers 1.7e5 (Mitalas & Sills) and ~1e6 (MSFC). The counter stops at 40,000+, not at a single disputed value.

claims.claim: + 8 MIN
claims.where: on-screen: sunlight lane, surface to you
claims.note: 8.14-8.42 min recomputed.

claims.claim: HYDROGEN → HELIUM
claims.note: MSFC 'consume hydrogen to form helium'.

claims.claim: CORE; CORE DRAWN AT 1/4 OF THE RADIUS
claims.where: on-screen: core marked on Sun photo
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%'; edge 'about 25% of the distance to the surface or 175,000 km from the center'. 175,000/695,700 = 0.252.

claims.claim: 4 MILLION+ TONNES, sub 'A SECOND · 4.7 MILLION US TONS'; running tag '<n> TONNES SO FAR' at 4.26 million tonnes per second of video
claims.note: NSSDC 4260e6 kg/s = 4.26 Mt/s ('4 MILLION+' true). 4.26e9 kg / 907.185 kg = 4.70 million short tons. The tag multiplies elapsed card time by 4.26e6 and rounds to the thousand, matching the stated rate.

claims.claim: 2 NEUTRINOS; 4 H → 1 He + 2 e⁺ + 2 ν (four H discs merge into one He disc, two ν arrows leave)
claims.note: BX-P eq. (1) '4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2 nu_e' with H for p (nuclei, as spoken). Two neutrinos per helium. Housekeeping only: the SOURCES block's closing 'Not spoken' paragraph quotes the label as '4 H → 1 He + 2 ν', while claim 6's entry and the code (index.tsx line 474) have the e⁺ version shown here; the on-screen string is correct.

claims.claim: BARELY INTERACT (straight teal lines through a photo of the Sun)
claims.note: MSFC 'pass right through the overlying layers'; BX-P 'almost undisturbed'.

claims.claim: ABOUT 2 SECONDS, running clock 0.0 S → 2.3 S
claims.note: R/c = 2.32 s, the time from the centre; the clock stops at 2.3 s (index.tsx EXIT_S = 2.32).

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES LATER (teal lines through a photo of a hand)
claims.note: 8.28 min mean recomputed; pass-through as claim 9.

claims.claim: TENS OF BILLIONS, sub 'PER CM² (0.16 SQ IN), PER SECOND'; square '1 cm² (ENLARGED)'; tag 'SCHEMATIC'
claims.note: BX-P pp flux (6.6 +- 0.7) x 10^10 cm^-2 s^-1. 1 cm^2 = 0.155 sq in -> 0.16. Enlargement and dot count are flagged as schematic (A6).

claims.claim: BOREXINO, ITALY (drawn sphere in a tank, tag 'SCHEMATIC')
claims.note: BX-P: liquid scintillator inner detector viewed by PMTs, 'Outside the inner detector, a water tank'; 'Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso, in central Italy'. Drawing labelled schematic.

claims.claim: ABOUT 140 A DAY, sub 'PER 100 TONNES (110 US TONS)'; schematic tally marks filling to 144 under '144 A DAY (AVERAGE)'
claims.note: BX-P eq. (2) 144 per day per 100 t. 100 t / 0.907185 t = 110.2 short tons. 'AVERAGE' is right: the 144 is a fitted mean rate over 408 live days (Jan 2012-Jun 2013), not a daily count; the tally is labelled schematic.

claims.claim: THE SLOW ROAD; OVER AND OVER
claims.note: SVS 'absorbed ... and emitted repeatedly'.

claims.claim: WITHIN ABOUT 10%; bars 'SUNLIGHT PREDICTS' 131 and 'BOREXINO COUNTED' 144 ± 16; axis 'PER DAY, PER 100 TONNES'
claims.note: BX-P: expected '131 +- 2 (d.100 t)^-1', measured '144 +- 13 (stat) +- 10 (syst)'; quadrature 16.4 -> 16. Bars are zero-based and linear (height = value x 3.6 px), so the chart does not exaggerate the gap. 144/131 = 1.10.

claims.claim: ABOUT THE SAME
claims.note: Within ~10% (0.8 sigma); BX-P 'consistent with expectation', 'stable'.

claims.claim: OLD NEWS; FRESH; THEY AGREE
claims.note: Restates claims 3, 9, 19.

claims.claim: NOT TO SCALE on every two-lane diagram (drawn Sun at top, photo of a hand standing for 'you' at bottom; straight teal and tangled coral lanes)
claims.note: A6: the deliberately non-to-scale sizes and distances are flagged on screen. Zones match MSFC (core to 0.25 R, radiative 0.25-0.70 R, convection above).
